source.text: Μετὰ δὲ ταῦτα ἀνέδειξεν ὁ κύριος καὶ ἑτέρους ἑβδομήκοντα δύο καὶ ἀπέστειλεν αὐτοὺς ἀνὰ δύο δύο πρὸ προσώπου αὐτοῦ εἰς πᾶσαν πόλιν καὶ τόπον οὗ ἤμελλεν αὐτὸς ἔρχεσθαι.

records.literal_gloss: After now these things appointed the Lord also others seventy-two and sent them two [by] two before [the] face of him into every town and place where was about he himself to come.

en.L: Now after these things the Lord appointed seventy-two others also, and sent them two by two ahead of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} into every town and place where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} was about to come.
en.B: After this the Lord appointed seventy-two others as well. He sent them out in pairs ahead of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, to every town and place {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was going to visit.
en.R: After this, the Lord chose seventy-two more of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers. He sent them out two at a time to go ahead of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They were to go to every town and place where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} planned to go.

fr.L: Après cela, le Seigneur désigna aussi soixante-douze autres, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les envoya deux par deux en avant de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dans toute ville et [tout] lieu où {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} devait {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} aller.
fr.B: Après cela, le Seigneur en désigna soixante-douze autres. Il les envoya deux à deux devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, dans toutes les villes et tous les endroits où {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} allait se rendre.
fr.R: Ensuite, le Seigneur a choisi soixante-douze autres de {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples. Il les a envoyés deux par deux pour qu’ils partent avant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Ils devaient aller dans chaque ville et chaque endroit où {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait l’intention d’aller.

decisions.choice: seventy-two (SBLGNT)
decisions.reason: The manuscripts are divided, and early ones stand on both sides. Some, among them Papyrus 75 and Codex Vaticanus, read seventy-two; others, among them Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Alexandrinus, and most later manuscripts, read seventy. The same split comes again at 10:17. Both numbers have Old Testament echoes: the nations listed in Genesis 10 number seventy in the Hebrew text and seventy-two in the Greek Old Testament, and Moses chose seventy elders, with two more who also prophesied in the camp (Numbers 11:16-26). Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: others also: more messengers, besides the Twelve sent out in 9:1-6
alternatives: others besides the messengers sent ahead in 9:52
decisions.reason: Jesus gave the Twelve much the same instructions in 9:1-5. He also sent messengers ahead of him in 9:52, and the wording may include them. Either way, the mission now widens beyond the Twelve.

decisions.choice: before his face: ahead of him, to prepare for his coming
decisions.reason: The phrase is a Hebrew way of saying "ahead of". It was used of the messengers in 9:52 and of the messenger God sends ahead in Malachi 3:1 (Luke 7:27). The seventy-two go to the places Jesus himself will visit.

decisions.choice: the Lord: Jesus
decisions.reason: Luke the narrator often calls Jesus "the Lord" (7:13, 19; 10:39, 41).

decisions.choice: more of his followers
decisions.reason: Readable says who the others were: they were disciples of Jesus (10:23).

decisions.choice: chose
decisions.reason: The verb means to name someone publicly for a task. Readable uses a common word.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R) (for the whole chapter)
decisions.reason: As in John and Mark: the passé simple is the normal tense of written narrative and suits a careful public reading; Readable uses the passé composé, as French is spoken and as young readers meet stories. Speech keeps its own tenses at every level, and the story Jesus tells in 10:30-35 is in the passé composé (style guide section 9).

decisions.choice: every French pronoun for God or Christ carries the deity_pronoun span, subject "il" included (for the whole chapter)
decisions.reason: As in Mark and Colossians. French must write the subject pronoun, so "il" for Jesus carries the span wherever the English "he" does, and so do pronouns French needs where English has none. A pronoun at the start of a sentence is written plainly with its capital ("Il les envoya").

source.text: ἔλεγεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτούς· Ὁ μὲν θερισμὸς πολύς, οἱ δὲ ἐργάται ὀλίγοι· δεήθητε οὖν τοῦ κυρίου τοῦ θερισμοῦ ὅπως ἐργάτας ἐκβάλῃ εἰς τὸν θερισμὸν αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: He was saying then to them, The indeed harvest [is] plentiful, but the workers few; ask therefore the Lord of the harvest that workers he may send out into the harvest of him.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was saying to them, "The harvest [is] plentiful, but the workers [are] few. Therefore ask the Lord of the harvest that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} send out workers into {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} harvest.
en.B: He told them, "There is a great harvest, but only a few workers. So plead with the Lord of the harvest to send workers out to bring in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} harvest.
en.R: Jesus told them, "There is a big harvest to gather, but there are only a few workers. So pray to the Lord who owns the harvest. Ask {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to send out more workers to bring in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} harvest.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur disait : « La moisson [est] abondante, mais les ouvriers [sont] peu nombreux. Priez donc le Seigneur de la moisson pour qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} envoie des ouvriers dans {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} moisson.
fr.B: Il leur dit : « Il y a beaucoup à moissonner, mais les ouvriers sont peu nombreux. Suppliez donc le Seigneur de la moisson d’envoyer des ouvriers pour rentrer {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} moisson.
fr.R: Jésus leur a dit : « Il y a une grande récolte à rentrer, mais il n’y a que peu d’ouvriers. Alors priez le Seigneur à qui appartient la récolte. Demandez-{{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} d’envoyer d’autres ouvriers pour rentrer {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} récolte.

decisions.choice: the harvest is plentiful: many people are ready to be gathered in for the kingdom of God
decisions.reason: The harvest is a picture of people being gathered in, as in John 4:35-38. Elsewhere a harvest can picture judgment (Joel 3:13), but here the workers gather people who will receive the message.

decisions.choice: the Lord of the harvest: God, who owns the harvest and sends its workers
decisions.reason: The owner of a harvest decides who works in it. The disciples are to ask him for workers. Yet Jesus is the one who sends the seventy-two (10:1, 3); God's work and his are one (10:16).

decisions.choice: send out: send with urgency, thrust out
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for driving out demons (9:40). Used of workers it stresses urgency: the harvest will not wait.

decisions.choice: ask: plead, pray
decisions.reason: The verb means to ask earnestly for something one needs. Luke uses it for prayer (5:12; 21:36).

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker at the start of the speech.

decisions.choice: the Lord who owns the harvest
decisions.reason: Readable says what "Lord of the harvest" means.

source.text: ὑπάγετε· ἰδοὺ ἀποστέλλω ὑμᾶς ὡς ἄρνας ἐν μέσῳ λύκων.

records.literal_gloss: Go; behold I send out you as lambs in [the] midst of wolves.

en.L: Go; look, I am sending you out as lambs in [the] midst of wolves.
en.B: Go on your way. I am sending you out like lambs among wolves.
en.R: Go now. I am sending you out like little lambs into a pack of wolves.

fr.L: Allez ; voici, je vous envoie comme des agneaux au milieu de loups.
fr.B: Allez. Je vous envoie comme des agneaux parmi des loups.
fr.R: Partez maintenant. Je vous envoie comme de petits agneaux au milieu d’une bande de loups.

decisions.choice: like lambs among wolves: without defense among people who may attack them
alternatives: among enemies who will all attack them
decisions.reason: Lambs cannot protect themselves from wolves. The messengers will go unarmed and without supplies (10:4) among people who may turn against them (10:10). Wolves are a picture of violent rulers in Ezekiel 22:27.

decisions.choice: I am sending: Jesus himself sends them as his messengers
decisions.reason: The verb is the one from which "apostle" comes. Those who hear them will be hearing Jesus (10:16).

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered as a separate word, or "now" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Luke uses this word to draw attention to what follows. "Behold" is old-fashioned; Literal says "look", and Balanced and Readable carry the force in the flow of the sentence, as in Matthew 1:20.

decisions.choice: voici (L)
decisions.reason: The English Literal says "look" because "behold" is old-fashioned. French "voici" is still current and is the natural way to point to what follows, so Literal keeps it here and in 10:19 and 10:25; Balanced and Readable carry the force in the sentence, as in English.

source.text: μὴ βαστάζετε βαλλάντιον, μὴ πήραν, μὴ ὑποδήματα, καὶ μηδένα κατὰ τὴν ὁδὸν ἀσπάσησθε.

records.literal_gloss: Not carry purse, nor bag, nor sandals, and no one along the road greet.

en.L: Do not carry a purse, nor a bag, nor sandals, and greet no one along the road.
en.B: Take no money bag, no pack and no sandals, and do not stop to greet anyone on the way.
en.R: Do not carry a money bag, a traveler's bag, or sandals. Do not stop to talk with people along the road.

fr.L: Ne portez ni bourse, ni sac, ni sandales, et ne saluez personne en chemin.
fr.B: N’emportez ni bourse, ni sac, ni sandales, et ne vous arrêtez pour saluer personne en chemin.
fr.R: Ne prenez pas de porte-monnaie, ni de sac de voyage, ni de sandales. Ne vous arrêtez pas pour discuter avec les gens sur la route.

decisions.choice: purse, bag, sandals: a money pouch, a bag for food and supplies, and footwear
decisions.reason: They are to go without the usual supplies and depend on the people who take them in, as the Twelve did (9:3). Jesus recalls this command in 22:35. The text does not say whether "sandals" means a spare pair.

decisions.choice: greet no one along the road: let nothing delay the task
decisions.reason: Greetings could be long and formal. The command stresses urgency, as when Elisha sent Gehazi ahead with orders not to greet anyone on the way (2 Kings 4:29).

decisions.choice: do not stop to greet (B); do not stop to talk with people (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the reason for the command plain: they are not to be held up on the way.

source.text: εἰς ἣν δ’ ἂν εἰσέλθητε οἰκίαν πρῶτον λέγετε· Εἰρήνη τῷ οἴκῳ τούτῳ.

records.literal_gloss: Into whatever now house you might enter, first say, Peace to the house this.

en.L: And into whatever house you enter, first say, 'Peace to this house.'
en.B: Whatever house you go into, begin by saying, 'Peace be on this household.'
en.R: When you go into a home, first say, 'May there be peace in this home.'

fr.L: Dans quelque maison que vous entriez, dites d’abord : “Paix à cette maison.”
fr.B: Dans toute maison où vous entrerez, commencez par dire : “Paix à cette maisonnée.”
fr.R: Quand vous entrez dans une maison, dites d’abord : “Que la paix soit dans cette maison !”

decisions.choice: Peace to this house: the usual greeting, here a real blessing
alternatives: a polite form of words only
decisions.reason: "Peace" was the ordinary greeting among Jews (1 Samuel 25:6). On the lips of Jesus's messengers it offers the peace that comes with the kingdom of God (1:79; 2:14).

decisions.choice: house: the household, the people who live there
decisions.reason: The blessing is for the people of the house, as 10:6 shows.

decisions.choice: May there be peace in this home
decisions.reason: Readable words the greeting as the wish it is.

source.text: καὶ ἐὰν ᾖ ἐκεῖ υἱὸς εἰρήνης, ἐπαναπαήσεται ἐπ’ αὐτὸν ἡ εἰρήνη ὑμῶν· εἰ δὲ μήγε, ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς ἀνακάμψει.

records.literal_gloss: And if there is there a son of peace, will rest upon him the peace of you; but if not, upon you it will return.

en.L: And if a son of peace is there, your peace will rest upon {{gender:that person|him}}; but if not, it will return to you.
en.B: If someone there is a person of peace, your peace will stay with {{gender:that person|him}}. If not, it will come back to you.
en.R: If someone there is ready to receive God's peace, your peace will stay with {{gender:that person|him}}. If not, your peace will come back to you.

fr.L: Et s’il y a là un fils de paix, votre paix reposera sur lui ; sinon, elle reviendra sur vous.
fr.B: S’il y a là quelqu’un qui accueille la paix, votre paix restera sur lui. Sinon, elle vous reviendra.
fr.R: Si quelqu’un, dans cette maison, est prêt à recevoir la paix de Dieu, votre paix restera sur lui. Sinon, votre paix reviendra vers vous.

decisions.choice: son of peace: a person who belongs to peace and is ready to welcome it
decisions.reason: "Son of" with a quality is a Hebrew way of describing someone marked by it ("sons of this age" and "sons of light", 16:8). Here it is someone open to the peace the messengers bring, who welcomes them (10:8).

decisions.choice: your peace will rest on him, or return to you: the blessing takes effect or comes back to the giver
alternatives: the messengers lose their peace if refused
decisions.reason: The greeting is pictured as a gift that settles on the one who receives it. If it is refused, it returns to the messengers, who lose nothing by it.

decisions.choice: a person of peace (B); someone ready to receive God's peace (R)
decisions.reason: "Son" here does not mean a male child; Balanced and Readable say what the idiom means. Readable spells out what being "of peace" means here.

decisions.choice: "sur lui" with no gender span
decisions.reason: English needs {{gender:that person|him}}. In French "lui" refers back to "un fils de paix" (L) or to "quelqu'un" (B, R), a generic pronoun that already means anyone, so no span is needed (style guide section 7).

source.text: ἐν αὐτῇ δὲ τῇ οἰκίᾳ μένετε, ἐσθίοντες καὶ πίνοντες τὰ παρ’ αὐτῶν, ἄξιος γὰρ ὁ ἐργάτης τοῦ μισθοῦ αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: In the same now house remain, eating and drinking the things from them; worthy [is] for the worker of the wages of him.

en.L: And remain in that same house, eating and drinking the things [provided] by them, for the worker [is] worthy of {{gender:their|his}} wages.
en.B: Stay in that one house, eating and drinking whatever they give you, since a worker has earned {{gender:their|his}} pay.
en.R: Stay in that same house. Eat and drink what the people there give you. People who work should be paid for their work.

fr.L: Et demeurez dans cette même maison, mangeant et buvant ce qui [vient] d’eux, car l’ouvrier est digne de son salaire.
fr.B: Restez dans cette maison-là, et mangez et buvez ce qu’on vous donne, car un ouvrier a droit à son salaire.
fr.R: Restez dans cette même maison. Mangez et buvez ce que les gens de la maison vous donnent. Ceux qui travaillent doivent être payés pour leur travail.

decisions.choice: remain in the same house: the house where they were first welcomed
decisions.reason: As in 9:4, they are to keep the lodging where they are first received until they leave the town.

decisions.choice: the worker is worthy of his wages: a saying about fair pay
decisions.reason: The law told employers to pay a worker on the same day (Deuteronomy 24:14-15). Paul quotes this saying as Scripture (1 Timothy 5:18) and draws the same point for those who preach (1 Corinthians 9:14). Food and lodging are the messengers' pay.

decisions.choice: the things from them: what the household provides
decisions.reason: They eat what their hosts give them, as in 10:8.

decisions.choice: People who work should be paid for their work.
alternatives: the worker is worthy of his wages
decisions.reason: Readable puts the saying in plain words, with a plural that needs no gender setting.

decisions.choice: "son salaire" with no gender span
alternatives: a gender span on the possessive
decisions.reason: English writes {{gender:their|his}} wages. The French possessive "son" agrees with "salaire", not with the worker, so it says nothing about the worker's sex and needs no span.

source.text: μὴ μεταβαίνετε ἐξ οἰκίας εἰς οἰκίαν.

records.literal_gloss: Not move from house to house.

en.L: Do not move from house to house.
en.B: Do not keep changing from one house to another.
en.R: Do not move around from one house to another.

fr.L: Ne passez pas de maison en maison.
fr.B: Ne changez pas sans cesse de maison.
fr.R: N’allez pas d’une maison à une autre.

decisions.choice: do not move: do not make a habit of moving to other lodgings
decisions.reason: The present tense with the negative forbids a practice: leaving the first host for a better offer. They may still visit other homes to bring the message.

source.text: καὶ εἰς ἣν ἂν πόλιν εἰσέρχησθε καὶ δέχωνται ὑμᾶς, ἐσθίετε τὰ παρατιθέμενα ὑμῖν, καὶ θεραπεύετε τοὺς ἐν αὐτῇ ἀσθενεῖς, καὶ λέγετε αὐτοῖς· Ἤγγικεν ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And into whatever city you might enter and they receive you, eat the things set before you, \v 9 and heal the in it sick, and say to them, Has come near upon you the kingdom of God.

en.L: And into whatever town you enter and they receive you, eat the things set before you, \v 9 and heal the sick in it, and say to them, 'The kingdom of God has come near to you.'
en.B: Whenever a town takes you in, eat whatever food they put in front of you. \v 9 Heal those in it who are sick, and tell the people, 'The kingdom of God has drawn near to you.'
en.R: When you go into a town and the people welcome you, eat the food they give you. \v 9 Heal the sick people in that town. Tell them, 'The kingdom of God has come close to you.'

fr.L: Et dans toute ville où vous entrerez et où l’on vous recevra, mangez ce qu’on met devant vous, \v 9 et guérissez les malades qui s’y trouvent, et dites-leur : “Le royaume de Dieu s’est approché de vous.”
fr.B: Quand une ville vous accueille, mangez ce qu’on vous sert. \v 9 Guérissez les malades qui s’y trouvent et dites aux gens : “Le royaume de Dieu est arrivé tout près de vous.”
fr.R: Quand vous entrez dans une ville et que les gens vous accueillent, mangez ce qu’ils vous donnent. \v 9 Guérissez les malades de cette ville. Dites-leur : “Le royaume de Dieu est venu tout près de vous.”

decisions.choice: eat what is set before you: accept the hospitality offered
decisions.reason: They are not to be particular about their food but take what their hosts serve. Paul gives the same rule for eating with others (1 Corinthians 10:27).

decisions.choice: has come near: God's rule is close at hand and already at work
decisions.reason: The verb means to draw near. The healings show that God's rule is breaking in (11:20), though its full coming is still ahead (21:31).

decisions.choice: city: town
decisions.reason: The word is used for any town, however small (9:5).

decisions.choice: takes you in
decisions.reason: Balanced uses an everyday phrase for receiving guests.

decisions.choice: le royaume de Dieu, every level (for the whole chapter)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's form. "Règne" would bring out God's rule as an activity, but "royaume" is the word French readers know and keeps the phrase the same across the Gospels; the meaning decision explains that God's rule is at work.

source.text: εἰς ἣν δ’ ἂν πόλιν εἰσέλθητε καὶ μὴ δέχωνται ὑμᾶς, ἐξελθόντες εἰς τὰς πλατείας αὐτῆς εἴπατε·

records.literal_gloss: Into whatever now city you might enter and not they receive you, having gone out into the streets of it say,

en.L: But into whatever town you enter and they do not receive you, go out into its streets and say,
en.B: But if you go into a town where the people do not welcome you, go out into its streets and say,
en.R: But a town may not welcome you. Then go out into its streets and say,

fr.L: Mais dans toute ville où vous entrerez et où l’on ne vous recevra pas, sortez dans ses rues et dites :
fr.B: Mais si vous entrez dans une ville où les gens ne vous accueillent pas, allez sur ses places et dites :
fr.R: Mais il se peut qu’une ville ne vous accueille pas. Alors allez dans ses rues et dites :

decisions.choice: its streets: the open places of the town, where all can hear
decisions.reason: The word means a wide street or open square. The messengers give their warning in public.

decisions.choice: do not receive you: turn away the messengers and their message
decisions.reason: Refusing the messengers is refusing Jesus, who sent them (10:16).

decisions.choice: two short sentences
decisions.reason: Readable states the case first and then the command.

source.text: Καὶ τὸν κονιορτὸν τὸν κολληθέντα ἡμῖν ἐκ τῆς πόλεως ὑμῶν εἰς τοὺς πόδας ἀπομασσόμεθα ὑμῖν· πλὴν τοῦτο γινώσκετε ὅτι ἤγγικεν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Even the dust that clung to us from the city of you on the feet we wipe off against you; yet this know, that has come near the kingdom of God.

en.L: 'Even the dust of your town that clings to our feet we wipe off against you. Yet know this, that the kingdom of God has come near.'
en.B: 'Against you we wipe off even the dust of your town that has stuck to our feet. All the same, be sure of this: the kingdom of God has come near.'
en.R: 'We are wiping even the dust of your town off our feet. It is a sign against you. But know this: the kingdom of God has come close.'

fr.L: “Même la poussière de votre ville qui s’est collée à nos pieds, nous l’essuyons contre vous. Cependant, sachez ceci : le royaume de Dieu s’est approché.”
fr.B: “Nous essuyons contre vous jusqu’à la poussière de votre ville qui s’est collée à nos pieds. Mais sachez-le bien : le royaume de Dieu est arrivé tout près.”
fr.R: “Nous essuyons même la poussière de votre ville qui est restée sur nos pieds. C’est un signe contre vous. Mais sachez ceci : le royaume de Dieu est venu tout près.”

decisions.choice: wiping off the dust: a public sign that the town is left to answer for itself
alternatives: a way of cleaning the feet
decisions.reason: The gesture says that the messengers take nothing of the town with them; they have done their part (9:5). Paul and Barnabas do it at Pisidian Antioch (Acts 13:51).

decisions.choice: against you: as evidence against you
decisions.reason: As in 9:5, the gesture is a witness that the town was told.

decisions.choice: yet know this: the kingdom comes near even to those who refuse it
alternatives: the kingdom has gone away from them
decisions.reason: The words to the welcoming town (10:9) are repeated without "to you". Refusing the message does not stop the kingdom from coming; the town will meet it as judgment (10:12).

decisions.choice: It is a sign against you.
decisions.reason: Readable makes "against you" its own sentence and says what the act means.

source.text: λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι Σοδόμοις ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐκείνῃ ἀνεκτότερον ἔσται ἢ τῇ πόλει ἐκείνῃ.

records.literal_gloss: I say to you that for Sodom in the day that more bearable it will be than for the city that.

en.L: I say to you that on that day it will be more bearable for Sodom than for that town.
en.B: I tell you, on that day Sodom will be better off than that town.
en.R: I tell you, on the day God judges, things will go easier for Sodom than for that town.

fr.L: Je vous dis que, en ce jour-là, ce sera plus supportable pour Sodome que pour cette ville-là.
fr.B: Je vous le dis : ce jour-là, Sodome s’en tirera mieux que cette ville.
fr.R: Je vous le dis : le jour où Dieu jugera, cela ira moins mal pour Sodome que pour cette ville.

decisions.choice: Sodom: the city God destroyed for its wickedness
decisions.reason: Sodom was the standing example of a city ripe for judgment (Genesis 18:20; 19:24-25; Isaiah 1:9-10; Luke 17:28-29). Its men also mistreated the messengers God sent there (Genesis 19:1-11).

decisions.choice: that day: the day of judgment
alternatives: the day the town refuses them
decisions.reason: "That day" is the prophets' way of speaking of the day when God judges (Isaiah 2:11-12; Luke 17:31; 21:34). Verse 14 calls it "the judgment".

decisions.choice: more bearable: easier to endure, less severe
decisions.reason: Sodom will still be judged, but the town that heard the message and turned it away will fare worse.

decisions.choice: will be better off (B); things will go easier (R)
decisions.reason: Everyday wording for "more bearable".

decisions.choice: on the day God judges
decisions.reason: Readable says which day is meant.

source.text: Οὐαί σοι, Χοραζίν· οὐαί σοι, Βηθσαϊδά· ὅτι εἰ ἐν Τύρῳ καὶ Σιδῶνι ἐγενήθησαν αἱ δυνάμεις αἱ γενόμεναι ἐν ὑμῖν, πάλαι ἂν ἐν σάκκῳ καὶ σποδῷ καθήμενοι μετενόησαν.

records.literal_gloss: Woe to you, Chorazin; woe to you, Bethsaida; because if in Tyre and Sidon had taken place the works of power that took place in you, long ago in sackcloth and ashes sitting they would have repented.

en.L: Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the works of power that took place in you had taken place in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago, sitting in sackcloth and ashes.
en.B: How terrible for you, Chorazin! How terrible for you, Bethsaida! If the mighty deeds that were done in you had been done in Tyre and Sidon, their people would long ago have sat down in sackcloth and ashes and repented.
en.R: How terrible for you, Chorazin! How terrible for you, Bethsaida! Great miracles were done in your towns. If those miracles had been done in Tyre and Sidon, the people there would have turned away from their sins long ago. They would have sat in rough clothes and ashes to show how sorry they were.

fr.L: Malheur à toi, Chorazin ! Malheur à toi, Bethsaïda ! Car si les actes de puissance qui ont eu lieu chez vous avaient eu lieu à Tyr et à Sidon, ils se seraient repentis depuis longtemps, assis dans le sac et la cendre.
fr.B: Malheur à toi, Chorazin ! Malheur à toi, Bethsaïda ! Si les miracles accomplis chez vous l’avaient été à Tyr et à Sidon, leurs habitants se seraient repentis depuis longtemps, vêtus de sacs et assis dans la cendre.
fr.R: Quel malheur pour toi, Chorazin ! Quel malheur pour toi, Bethsaïda ! De grands miracles ont été faits dans vos villes. Si ces miracles avaient été faits à Tyr et à Sidon, les gens de là-bas se seraient détournés de leurs péchés depuis longtemps. Ils se seraient assis dans des habits de toile grossière et dans la cendre pour montrer leur regret.

decisions.choice: Chorazin and Bethsaida: towns near Capernaum, at the north end of the Sea of Galilee
decisions.reason: Jesus fed the five thousand near Bethsaida (9:10). Chorazin lay in the hills a short way north of Capernaum. The Gospels tell of no miracle in Chorazin; the saying shows that Jesus did more than they record (John 21:25).

decisions.choice: Tyre and Sidon: Gentile cities on the coast north of Galilee
decisions.reason: The prophets spoke against them for their pride and wealth (Isaiah 23; Ezekiel 26-28). Yet people from that coast came to hear Jesus (6:17).

decisions.choice: sitting in sackcloth and ashes: signs of grief and repentance
decisions.reason: Sackcloth was rough cloth woven from goat's hair. People who mourned or repented wore it and sat in ashes, as the king of Nineveh did when Jonah preached (Jonah 3:6; Daniel 9:3).

decisions.choice: works of power: miracles
decisions.reason: The word means power, and in the plural, acts that show power (19:37; Acts 2:22).

decisions.choice: Woe to you (L); How terrible for you (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Woe" is rarely heard in everyday speech. Literal keeps the old cry; Balanced and Readable say what it means. The same wording as the woes of 6:24-26.

decisions.choice: turned away from their sins
decisions.reason: Readable explains repenting, as it does in 3:3 and 5:32.

decisions.choice: Great miracles were done in your towns. If those miracles had been done...
decisions.reason: Readable first states what happened, then the comparison.

decisions.choice: Malheur à toi (L, B); Quel malheur pour toi (R)
alternatives: Quel malheur pour toi at Balanced too, as the English "How terrible for you"
decisions.reason: The term sheet keeps "Malheur à" at Literal and Balanced: unlike English "woe", it is still understood and used in French. Readable follows the English with an exclamation young readers hear as a lament. "Toi" because each town is addressed as one.

decisions.choice: se repentir (L, B); se détourner de leurs péchés (R)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's forms; Readable follows the English "turned away from their sins".

source.text: πλὴν Τύρῳ καὶ Σιδῶνι ἀνεκτότερον ἔσται ἐν τῇ κρίσει ἢ ὑμῖν.

records.literal_gloss: But for Tyre and Sidon more bearable it will be in the judgment than for you.

en.L: But it will be more bearable for Tyre and Sidon in the judgment than for you.
en.B: But at the judgment Tyre and Sidon will be better off than you.
en.R: When God judges, things will go easier for Tyre and Sidon than for you.

fr.L: Cependant, pour Tyr et Sidon, ce sera plus supportable lors du jugement que pour vous.
fr.B: Mais au jugement, Tyr et Sidon s’en tireront mieux que vous.
fr.R: Quand Dieu jugera, cela ira moins mal pour Tyr et Sidon que pour vous.

decisions.choice: the judgment: God's final judgment
decisions.reason: This is the day of 10:12. Those who saw and heard Jesus will be judged by what they were shown (11:31-32; 12:48).

decisions.choice: than for you: the people of Chorazin and Bethsaida
decisions.reason: Jesus still speaks to the towns of 10:13, as if they were present.

decisions.choice: will be better off (B); things will go easier (R)
decisions.reason: As in 10:12.

decisions.choice: When God judges
decisions.reason: Readable says who judges.

source.text: καὶ σύ, Καφαρναούμ, μὴ ἕως οὐρανοῦ ὑψωθήσῃ;

records.literal_gloss: And you, Capernaum, not to heaven will you be lifted up?

en.L: And you, Capernaum, will you be lifted up to heaven?
en.B: And you, Capernaum, will you be raised as high as heaven?
en.R: And you, people of Capernaum, do you think you will be lifted up to heaven?

fr.L: Et toi, Capharnaüm, seras-tu élevée jusqu’au ciel ?
fr.B: Et toi, Capharnaüm, vas-tu être élevée aussi haut que le ciel ?
fr.R: Et vous, les habitants de Capharnaüm, pensez-vous que vous serez élevés jusqu’au ciel ?

decisions.choice: a question expecting the answer no
alternatives: a statement: you will be lifted up
decisions.reason: The Greek question is worded to expect "No". Capernaum had been Jesus's base (4:31; 7:1) and had seen much of his work, and it may have thought itself raised high by it.

decisions.choice: will you be lifted up to heaven? (SBLGNT)
alternatives: you who have been lifted up to heaven
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts have a statement about the town instead of a question; the question has strong early support. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: lifted up to heaven: echoing Isaiah 14:13
decisions.reason: In Isaiah the king of Babylon says in his heart that he will climb up to heaven (Isaiah 14:13). The next sentence finishes the echo.

decisions.choice: people of Capernaum; do you think
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the town means its people and that the question challenges what they think of themselves.

decisions.choice: vous, les habitants de Capharnaüm (R)
decisions.reason: Readable addresses the people of the town, as the English does, so French uses "vous" for them; Literal and Balanced keep "toi" for the town, which is feminine in French ("élevée").

source.text: ἕως τοῦ ᾅδου καταβιβασθήσῃ.

records.literal_gloss: To Hades you will be brought down.

en.L: To Hades you will be brought down.
en.B: No, you will be brought down to Hades.
en.R: No, God will bring you down to the place of the dead.

fr.L: Jusqu’à l’Hadès tu seras abaissée.
fr.B: Non, tu seras précipitée jusqu’au séjour des morts.
fr.R: Non, Dieu vous fera descendre jusqu’au séjour des morts.

decisions.choice: Hades: the place of the dead
decisions.reason: The Greek Old Testament uses the word for Sheol, the world of the dead below the earth (Psalm 16:10; Acts 2:27). Here it is the opposite of heaven: the lowest place, a picture of utter humbling under judgment.

decisions.choice: brought down to Hades: echoing Isaiah 14:15
decisions.reason: Isaiah tells the king of Babylon, who wanted to climb to heaven, that he will be brought down to Sheol, to the depths of the pit (Isaiah 14:13-15). The proud town will share that fate.

decisions.choice: you will be brought down (SBLGNT)
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts have the passive "you will be brought down", the wording of the Greek of Isaiah 14:15; some early ones, among them Papyrus 75 and Codex Vaticanus, have "you will go down". The meaning is much the same. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: No,
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable answer the question of the previous sentence.

decisions.choice: God will bring you down to the place of the dead
alternatives: you will be brought down to Hades
decisions.reason: Readable explains Hades and names God as the one who brings the town down, which the passive implies.

decisions.choice: l’Hadès (L); le séjour des morts (B, R)
alternatives: l’Hadès at Balanced, as the English
decisions.reason: The term sheet's forms. "Le séjour des morts" is the established French phrase for the place of the dead, so Balanced can use it where the English keeps the name; "l'enfer" would suggest a place of punishment, which the word does not say here.

source.text: Ὁ ἀκούων ὑμῶν ἐμοῦ ἀκούει, καὶ ὁ ἀθετῶν ὑμᾶς ἐμὲ ἀθετεῖ· ὁ δὲ ἐμὲ ἀθετῶν ἀθετεῖ τὸν ἀποστείλαντά με.

records.literal_gloss: The one hearing you me hears, and the one rejecting you me rejects; and the one me rejecting rejects the one having sent me.

en.L: The one who hears you hears {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and the one who rejects you rejects {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; and the one who rejects {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} rejects the one who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."
en.B: Anyone who listens to you listens to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. Anyone who turns you away turns {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} away, and anyone who turns {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} away turns away the one who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."
en.R: When people listen to you, they are listening to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. When people turn you away, they are turning {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} away. And anyone who turns {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} away is turning away God, who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

fr.L: Celui qui vous écoute {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}écoute, et celui qui vous rejette {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} rejette ; et celui qui {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} rejette rejette celui qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a envoyé. »
fr.B: Qui vous écoute {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}écoute. Qui vous repousse {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} repousse, et qui {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} repousse repousse celui qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a envoyé. »
fr.R: Quand les gens vous écoutent, c’est {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} qu’ils écoutent. Quand les gens vous refusent, c’est {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} qu’ils refusent. Et celui qui {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} refuse, c’est Dieu qu’il refuse, Dieu qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a envoyé. »

decisions.choice: hearing you is hearing me: the messengers speak for Jesus
alternatives: the messengers speak only for themselves
decisions.reason: A messenger stood for the one who sent him. To welcome or refuse Jesus's messengers is to welcome or refuse him (9:48; John 13:20).

decisions.choice: the one who sent me: God
decisions.reason: Jesus himself was sent by God (4:18, 43; 9:48).

decisions.choice: reject: refuse, set aside as worthless
decisions.reason: The verb means to treat as void or refuse to accept, as the Pharisees refused God's purpose (7:30).

decisions.choice: turns away
decisions.reason: An everyday phrase for refusing someone.

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Readable names the sender.

source.text: Ὑπέστρεψαν δὲ οἱ ἑβδομήκοντα δύο μετὰ χαρᾶς λέγοντες· Κύριε, καὶ τὰ δαιμόνια ὑποτάσσεται ἡμῖν ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί σου.

records.literal_gloss: Returned then the seventy-two with joy saying, Lord, even the demons are subject to us in the name of you.

en.L: And the seventy-two returned with joy, saying, "Lord, even the demons submit to us in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name!"
en.B: The seventy-two came back full of joy. "Lord," they said, "when we use {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name, even the demons obey us!"
en.R: Later the seventy-two followers came back filled with joy. They said, "Lord, even the demons obey us when we use {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name!"

fr.L: Et les soixante-douze revinrent avec joie, disant : « Seigneur, même les démons nous sont soumis en {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} nom ! »
fr.B: Les soixante-douze revinrent pleins de joie. « Seigneur, dirent-ils, quand nous agissons en {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} nom, même les démons nous obéissent ! »
fr.R: Plus tard, les soixante-douze disciples sont revenus, remplis de joie. Ils ont dit : « Seigneur, même les démons nous obéissent quand nous utilisons {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} nom ! »

decisions.choice: seventy-two (SBLGNT)
decisions.reason: The same variant as in 10:1, with the manuscripts divided in the same way. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: submit: are made subject, obey
decisions.reason: The verb means to be placed under someone's authority. The demons had to do what they were told.

decisions.choice: in your name: by your authority, calling on your name
decisions.reason: They drove out demons by commanding them in Jesus's name (9:49; Acts 16:18).

decisions.choice: even: more than they expected
decisions.reason: They had been told to heal the sick (10:9); power over demons is more than they were promised.

decisions.choice: Later; followers
decisions.reason: Readable marks the passing of time and says who the seventy-two were.

source.text: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτοῖς· Ἐθεώρουν τὸν Σατανᾶν ὡς ἀστραπὴν ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ πεσόντα.

records.literal_gloss: He said then to them, I was watching Satan as lightning out of heaven having fallen.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "I was watching Satan fall from heaven like lightning.
en.B: He told them, "I watched Satan fall from heaven like a flash of lightning.
en.R: Jesus answered, "I saw Satan fall from heaven as fast as lightning.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur dit : « Je regardais Satan tomber du ciel comme un éclair.
fr.B: Il leur répondit : « J’ai vu Satan tomber du ciel comme un éclair.
fr.R: Jésus a répondu : « J’ai vu Satan tomber du ciel, rapide comme l’éclair.

decisions.choice: I was watching: Jesus saw it while the seventy-two were at work
alternatives: a vision of the end of time
decisions.reason: The past continuous tense describes what Jesus was seeing. The power of the seventy-two over demons showed that Satan's rule was being broken. Luke does not say whether it was a vision.

decisions.choice: fall from heaven: possibly echoing Isaiah 14:12
decisions.reason: Isaiah pictures the proud king of Babylon as the morning star fallen from heaven (Isaiah 14:12). Jesus uses a like picture for Satan's sudden defeat. Lightning is swift and seen by all.

decisions.choice: Satan: the adversary, the devil
decisions.reason: The name means "adversary" or "accuser" in Hebrew (Job 1:6). Luke also calls him the devil (4:2).

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker.

decisions.choice: as fast as lightning
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture points to: the fall was sudden.

source.text: ἰδοὺ δέδωκα ὑμῖν τὴν ἐξουσίαν τοῦ πατεῖν ἐπάνω ὄφεων καὶ σκορπίων, καὶ ἐπὶ πᾶσαν τὴν δύναμιν τοῦ ἐχθροῦ, καὶ οὐδὲν ὑμᾶς οὐ μὴ ἀδικήσῃ.

records.literal_gloss: Behold I have given you the authority to tread upon serpents and scorpions, and upon all the power of the enemy, and nothing you not not will harm.

en.L: Look, I have given you the authority to tread on snakes and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy, and nothing will harm you in any way.
en.B: I have given you authority to trample snakes and scorpions underfoot, and authority over all the enemy's power. Nothing at all will be able to hurt you.
en.R: I have given you power to step on snakes and scorpions. I have given you power over everything the enemy can do. Nothing will hurt you at all.

fr.L: Voici, je vous ai donné l’autorité de marcher sur les serpents et les scorpions, et sur toute la puissance de l’ennemi, et rien ne vous nuira en aucune façon.
fr.B: Je vous ai donné autorité pour écraser sous vos pieds serpents et scorpions, et autorité sur toute la puissance de l’ennemi. Rien ne pourra vous faire le moindre mal.
fr.R: Je vous ai donné le pouvoir de marcher sur les serpents et les scorpions. Je vous ai donné le pouvoir sur tout ce que l’ennemi peut faire. Rien ne vous fera de mal, rien du tout.

decisions.choice: tread on snakes and scorpions: recalling Psalm 91:13 and Deuteronomy 8:15
alternatives: only a promise of safety from real animals
decisions.reason: God promises the one who trusts in him that he will tread on the lion and the serpent (Psalm 91:13). Snakes and scorpions were dangers of the wilderness (Deuteronomy 8:15). They stand for the powers of evil as well as for real danger (Acts 28:3-6).

decisions.choice: the enemy: Satan
decisions.reason: Satan has just been named (10:18). He is the enemy of God and of God's people (Matthew 13:39).

decisions.choice: nothing will harm you at all: a strong double negative
decisions.reason: The Greek piles up negatives for emphasis. It promises that the enemy cannot defeat them, not that they will never suffer; Jesus later warns that some will be put to death, yet not a hair of their head will perish (21:16-18).

decisions.choice: I have given: a gift that stands
decisions.reason: The perfect tense means the authority has been given and remains theirs.

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered as a separate word, or "now" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Luke uses this word to draw attention to what follows. "Behold" is old-fashioned; Literal says "look", and Balanced and Readable carry the force in the flow of the sentence, as in Matthew 1:20.

decisions.choice: power (for both words)
decisions.reason: Readable uses "power" for both the right to act and the strength to act, since the difference is hard to put simply.

source.text: πλὴν ἐν τούτῳ μὴ χαίρετε ὅτι τὰ πνεύματα ὑμῖν ὑποτάσσεται, χαίρετε δὲ ὅτι τὰ ὀνόματα ὑμῶν ἐγγέγραπται ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς.

records.literal_gloss: Yet in this not rejoice, that the spirits to you are subject, rejoice however that the names of you have been written in the heavens.

en.L: Nevertheless, do not rejoice in this, that the spirits submit to you, but rejoice that your names have been written in the heavens."
en.B: But do not be glad because the spirits obey you. Be glad instead that your names stand written in heaven."
en.R: But do not be happy because the spirits obey you. Be happy because your names are written in heaven."

fr.L: Cependant, ne vous réjouissez pas de ceci, que les esprits vous sont soumis, mais réjouissez-vous de ce que vos noms ont été inscrits dans les cieux. »
fr.B: Pourtant, ne vous réjouissez pas de ce que les esprits vous obéissent ; réjouissez-vous plutôt de ce que vos noms sont inscrits dans le ciel. »
fr.R: Mais ne soyez pas heureux parce que les esprits vous obéissent. Soyez heureux parce que vos noms sont écrits dans le ciel. »

decisions.choice: the spirits: the demons of 10:17
decisions.reason: Luke calls demons unclean or evil spirits (4:33; 8:2).

decisions.choice: your names are written in heaven: they belong to God's people for ever
alternatives: their names are honored on earth
decisions.reason: Scripture speaks of a book in which God writes the names of his people (Exodus 32:32; Daniel 12:1; Philippians 4:3). The perfect tense says the names stand written.

decisions.choice: do not rejoice ... but rejoice: the greater reason for joy
alternatives: they must take no pleasure in their power
decisions.reason: "Not this, but that" is a Hebrew way of setting one thing far above another. Jesus points them from what they can do to what God has done for them.

decisions.choice: be glad (B); be happy (R)
decisions.reason: Everyday words for rejoicing.

decisions.choice: heaven
decisions.reason: The plural follows the Hebrew way of speaking of heaven; Balanced and Readable use the singular, as English usually does.

decisions.choice: réjouissez-vous (B)
decisions.reason: English Balanced says "be glad" because "rejoice" sounds churchy. French "se réjouir" is ordinary careful French, so Balanced keeps it; Readable says "soyez heureux", as the English "be happy".

source.text: Ἐν αὐτῇ τῇ ὥρᾳ ἠγαλλιάσατο τῷ πνεύματι τῷ ἁγίῳ καὶ εἶπεν· Ἐξομολογοῦμαί σοι, πάτερ κύριε τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καὶ τῆς γῆς, ὅτι ἀπέκρυψας ταῦτα ἀπὸ σοφῶν καὶ συνετῶν, καὶ ἀπεκάλυψας αὐτὰ νηπίοις· ναί, ὁ πατήρ, ὅτι οὕτως εὐδοκία ἐγένετο ἔμπροσθέν σου.

records.literal_gloss: In the same hour he rejoiced in the Spirit the Holy and said, I praise you, Father, Lord of the heaven and of the earth, that you hid these things from wise and understanding and revealed them to little children; yes, Father, for thus well-pleasing it was before you.

en.L: In that same hour {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rejoiced in the Holy Spirit and said, "I praise {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} hid these things from [the] wise and understanding and revealed them to little children; yes, Father, for so it was well-pleasing before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.
en.B: At that very time Jesus rejoiced in the Holy Spirit and said, "I praise {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have kept these things hidden from the wise and the clever, and have made them known to little children. Yes, Father, for this is what seemed good to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.
en.R: At that time Jesus was moved by the Holy Spirit and was very glad. He said, "Father, Lord of heaven and earth, I praise {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. You have hidden these things from people who are wise and clever. But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have shown them to people who are like little children. Yes, Father, this is what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} wanted to do.

fr.L: À cette heure même, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} exulta dans l’Esprit Saint et dit : « Je {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} loue, Père, Seigneur du ciel et de la terre, parce que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as caché ces choses aux sages et aux intelligents et que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} les as révélées aux petits enfants ; oui, Père, car c’est ainsi que cela a été agréable devant {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}.
fr.B: Au même moment, Jésus exulta de joie dans l’Esprit Saint et dit : « Je {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} loue, Père, Seigneur du ciel et de la terre, parce que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as tenu ces choses cachées aux sages et aux gens habiles, et que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} les as fait connaître aux petits enfants. Oui, Père, c’est ce qui {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}a semblé bon.
fr.R: À ce moment-là, l’Esprit Saint a rempli Jésus d’une grande joie. Il a dit : « Père, Seigneur du ciel et de la terre, je {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} loue. Tu as caché ces choses aux gens sages et intelligents. Mais {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} les as montrées à ceux qui sont comme de petits enfants. Oui, Père, c’est cela que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as voulu faire.

decisions.choice: rejoiced in the Holy Spirit (SBLGNT)
alternatives: rejoiced in the spirit (his own spirit)
Jesus rejoiced in the Holy Spirit
decisions.reason: Manuscripts differ here. Many early ones read "the Holy Spirit", with or without the word "in"; many later ones have "in the spirit" without "Holy", meaning Jesus's own spirit, and some name Jesus. The SBLGNT reads "the Holy Spirit" without "in". Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: rejoiced in the Holy Spirit: was filled with exultant joy that came from the Spirit
alternatives: was glad in his own spirit
decisions.reason: The verb means to rejoice greatly, as Mary rejoices in God (1:47). Luke ties Jesus's joy to the Spirit, as he tied his ministry to the Spirit (4:1, 14, 18).

decisions.choice: I praise you: I openly acknowledge you with thanks
alternatives: I confess my sins to you
decisions.reason: The verb means to declare openly. Spoken to God it means to praise him and agree with what he has done (Romans 15:9).

decisions.choice: these things: what the disciples are seeing of the kingdom of God
decisions.reason: "These things" is not spelled out. In context it is the meaning of Jesus's work and the coming of the kingdom (10:9, 18, 23-24).

decisions.choice: little children: people without learning or standing
decisions.reason: The word means infants. Here it stands for people like the disciples, who had no training in the law (Acts 4:13), in contrast with those counted wise.

decisions.choice: well-pleasing: what God was pleased to choose
decisions.reason: The word means good pleasure or gracious will, as in "people of his good pleasure" (2:14).

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus at the start of a new section.

decisions.choice: short sentences; "moved by the Holy Spirit and was very glad"
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the prayer into short sentences and says plainly how the Spirit and Jesus's joy are connected, following the meaning decision above.

decisions.choice: l’Esprit Saint (for the whole chapter)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's form, as in John and Mark. Readable makes the Spirit the source of Jesus's joy ("l'Esprit Saint a rempli Jésus d'une grande joie"), following the meaning decision as the English Readable does.

source.text: πάντα μοι παρεδόθη ὑπὸ τοῦ πατρός μου, καὶ οὐδεὶς γινώσκει τίς ἐστιν ὁ υἱὸς εἰ μὴ ὁ πατήρ, καὶ τίς ἐστιν ὁ πατὴρ εἰ μὴ ὁ υἱὸς καὶ ᾧ ἐὰν βούληται ὁ υἱὸς ἀποκαλύψαι.

records.literal_gloss: All things to me were handed over by the Father of me, and no one knows who is the Son except the Father, and who is the Father except the Son and to whom if wishes the Son to reveal.

en.L: All things have been handed over to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father, and no one knows who the Son is except the Father, and who the Father is except the Son and [anyone] to whom the Son wishes to reveal [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}]."
en.B: My Father has put all things into {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hands. Who the Son is, only the Father knows; and who the Father is, only the Son knows, along with anyone to whom the Son is willing to make {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} known."
en.R: My Father has given everything to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. Only the Father knows who the Son is. And only the Son knows who the Father is. The Son also shows who the Father is to the people {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} chooses."

fr.L: Toutes choses {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}ont été remises par {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père, et personne ne connaît qui est le Fils, sinon le Père, ni qui est le Père, sinon le Fils et [celui] à qui le Fils veut [{{deity_pronoun:le|Le}}] révéler. »
fr.B: Mon Père a tout remis entre {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} mains. Qui est le Fils, le Père seul le sait ; et qui est le Père, seul le Fils le sait, ainsi que celui à qui le Fils veut bien {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} faire connaître. »
fr.R: Mon Père {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a tout donné. Seul le Père sait qui est le Fils. Et seul le Fils sait qui est le Père. Le Fils montre aussi qui est le Père aux personnes qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} choisit. »

decisions.choice: all things handed over: all authority and all knowledge of the Father
alternatives: only the teaching he passes on
decisions.reason: The Father has given all things into the Son's hand (John 3:35; Matthew 28:18). In context this includes the knowledge of God that the Son reveals.

decisions.choice: knows: a close, personal knowing between the Father and the Son
decisions.reason: Only the Father truly knows the Son, and only the Son truly knows the Father (John 10:15). Jesus speaks of himself as "the Son".

decisions.choice: to reveal him: the Father
decisions.reason: The object is not stated; the sentence implies it is the Father, whom only the Son knows.

decisions.choice: no introduction (SBLGNT)
alternatives: And turning to the disciples, he said
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts begin the verse with these words, probably taken from 10:23; early manuscripts do not have them. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: My Father has put all things into my hands (B); My Father has given everything to me (R)
alternatives: All things have been handed over to me by my Father
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the Father the subject, which is plainer than the passive.

source.text: Καὶ στραφεὶς πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς κατ’ ἰδίαν εἶπεν· Μακάριοι οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ οἱ βλέποντες ἃ βλέπετε.

records.literal_gloss: And having turned to the disciples privately he said, Blessed the eyes that see what you see.

en.L: And turning to the disciples, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said privately, "Blessed [are] the eyes that see the things you see.
en.B: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} turned to the disciples and said to them alone, "Blessed are the eyes that are seeing what you see.
en.R: Then Jesus turned to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers and spoke to them alone. He said, "How blessed are the eyes that see what you are seeing!

fr.L: Et, se tournant vers les disciples, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit en particulier : « Heureux les yeux qui voient ce que vous voyez.
fr.B: Puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} se tourna vers les disciples et leur dit, à eux seuls : « Ils sont heureux, les yeux qui voient ce que vous voyez.
fr.R: Puis Jésus s’est tourné vers {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples, et il leur a parlé à eux seuls. Il leur a dit : « Quel bonheur pour les yeux qui voient ce que vous voyez !

decisions.choice: privately: to the disciples alone
decisions.reason: Jesus turns from his prayer to speak to the disciples apart from the crowd.

decisions.choice: blessed: happy and favored by God
decisions.reason: As in the Beatitudes (6:20-22), the word speaks of the good God gives.

decisions.choice: the eyes that see: the people who see
decisions.reason: The eyes stand for the people themselves. What they see is Jesus's work and the coming of the kingdom of God.

decisions.choice: How blessed
decisions.reason: As in 6:20-22, Readable makes the saying an exclamation.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus.

decisions.choice: Heureux (L, B); Quel bonheur pour (R)
decisions.reason: "Bienheureux" now sounds like church language; "heureux" is the plain word and, in this kind of saying, still carries the sense of being favored by God (m2). Readable makes the saying an exclamation, as the English does. Jesus's disciples are "disciples" at every level, where English Readable says "followers".

source.text: λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν ὅτι πολλοὶ προφῆται καὶ βασιλεῖς ἠθέλησαν ἰδεῖν ἃ ὑμεῖς βλέπετε καὶ οὐκ εἶδαν, καὶ ἀκοῦσαι ἃ ἀκούετε καὶ οὐκ ἤκουσαν.

records.literal_gloss: I say for to you that many prophets and kings wanted to see what you see and not saw, and to hear what you hear and not heard.

en.L: For I say to you that many prophets and kings wanted to see what you see and did not see [it], and to hear what you hear and did not hear [it]."
en.B: I tell you, many prophets and kings longed to see the things you are seeing, yet never saw them; they longed to hear the things you are hearing, yet never heard them."
en.R: I tell you, many prophets and kings in the past wished they could see what you see now. But they never saw it. They wished they could hear what you hear. But they never heard it."

fr.L: Car je vous dis que beaucoup de prophètes et de rois ont voulu voir ce que vous voyez, et ne [l’]ont pas vu, et entendre ce que vous entendez, et ne [l’]ont pas entendu. »
fr.B: Je vous le dis : beaucoup de prophètes et de rois ont désiré voir ce que vous voyez, mais ne l’ont jamais vu ; ils ont désiré entendre ce que vous entendez, mais ne l’ont jamais entendu. »
fr.R: Je vous le dis : autrefois, beaucoup de prophètes et de rois auraient voulu voir ce que vous voyez maintenant. Mais ils ne l’ont jamais vu. Ils auraient voulu entendre ce que vous entendez. Mais ils ne l’ont jamais entendu. »

decisions.choice: prophets and kings: the faithful of Israel's past who waited for God's promises
decisions.reason: The prophets looked ahead to a salvation they did not live to see (1 Peter 1:10-12; Hebrews 11:13). David and other kings received promises about the coming king (1:32-33).

decisions.choice: for: giving the reason the disciples are blessed
decisions.reason: The disciples see what generations before them longed for.

decisions.choice: in the past; now
decisions.reason: Readable makes the contrast in time plain.

source.text: Καὶ ἰδοὺ νομικός τις ἀνέστη ἐκπειράζων αὐτὸν λέγων· Διδάσκαλε, τί ποιήσας ζωὴν αἰώνιον κληρονομήσω;

records.literal_gloss: And behold an expert in the law certain stood up testing him saying, Teacher, what having done eternal life will I inherit?

en.L: And look, a certain expert in the law stood up, testing {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying, "Teacher, by doing what will I inherit eternal life?"
en.B: Then an expert in the law stood up to put Jesus to the test. "Teacher," he said, "what do I have to do to inherit eternal life?"
en.R: One day an expert in God's law stood up to test Jesus. He asked, "Teacher, what must I do to have eternal life?"

fr.L: Et voici, un certain expert de la Loi se leva pour {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} mettre à l’épreuve, disant : « Maître, en faisant quoi hériterai-je de la vie éternelle ? »
fr.B: Alors un expert de la Loi se leva pour mettre Jésus à l’épreuve. « Maître, demanda-t-il, que dois-je faire pour hériter de la vie éternelle ? »
fr.R: Un jour, un expert de la Loi s’est levé pour mettre Jésus à l’épreuve. Il a demandé : « Maître, qu’est-ce que je dois faire pour avoir la vie éternelle ? »

decisions.choice: expert in the law: a man trained in the law of Moses, much like the scribes
decisions.reason: Luke uses this word for the experts who taught and applied God's law (7:30; 11:45-52).

decisions.choice: testing him: putting him to the test, to see how he would answer
decisions.reason: The same verb is used when Jesus refuses to put God to the test (4:12). The expert wants to see whether Jesus's answer will stand up; his next question shows he also wanted to defend himself (10:29).

decisions.choice: inherit eternal life: receive the life of the age to come
decisions.reason: "Inherit" was used of Israel receiving the promised land (Deuteronomy 4:1). Eternal life is the life of the age to come (Daniel 12:2; Luke 18:18, 30). The question assumes there is something one must do to receive it.

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered as a separate word, or "now" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Luke uses this word to draw attention to what follows. "Behold" is old-fashioned; Literal says "look", and Balanced and Readable carry the force in the flow of the sentence, as in Matthew 1:20.

decisions.choice: expert in God's law (R); expert in the law (L, B)
decisions.reason: As in 7:30. Today "lawyer" suggests courts and contracts.

decisions.choice: have
decisions.reason: Readable uses a simpler verb; the meaning decision explains "inherit".

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus, since "him" has no clear reference at the start of a new section.

decisions.choice: un expert de la Loi (every level)
decisions.reason: "Docteur de la Loi" is the traditional phrase, but "docteur" now means a physician to most readers; "légiste" suggests forensic medicine. "Expert" says what the man was; As in 7:30; Readable uses the same phrase as for the scribes. "La Loi" is capitalised for the Law of Moses (style guide section 9), here and in 10:26.

source.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτόν· Ἐν τῷ νόμῳ τί γέγραπται;

records.literal_gloss: And he said to him, In the law what has been written?

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to him, "What has been written in the law?
en.B: Jesus answered him, "What stands written in the law?
en.R: Jesus answered, "What does God's law say?

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} lui dit : « Qu’est-il écrit dans la Loi ?
fr.B: Jésus lui répondit : « Qu’est-ce qui est écrit dans la Loi ?
fr.R: Jésus a répondu : « Que dit la Loi de Dieu ?

decisions.choice: the law: the law of Moses, the first five books of Scripture
decisions.reason: As in 2:22-24, the law is the law God gave through Moses.

decisions.choice: Jesus answers with a question
decisions.reason: He sends the expert back to the Scripture he knows, and lets him answer his own question.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speaker.

decisions.choice: God's law
decisions.reason: Readable says whose law is meant.

source.text: πῶς ἀναγινώσκεις;

records.literal_gloss: How read you?

en.L: How do you read [it]?"
en.B: What do you read there?"
en.R: What do you understand it to say?"

fr.L: Comment lis-tu ? »
fr.B: Qu’y lis-tu ? »
fr.R: Comment la comprends-tu ? »

decisions.choice: how do you read it: what does it say, as you read it
decisions.reason: The question asks what the man finds in Scripture. He answers by quoting it.

decisions.choice: What (B); What do you understand it to say (R)
decisions.reason: "How" would suggest a question about method; Balanced and Readable ask what he finds there.

source.text: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν· Ἀγαπήσεις κύριον τὸν θεόν σου ἐξ ὅλης τῆς καρδίας σου καὶ ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ ψυχῇ σου καὶ ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ ἰσχύϊ σου καὶ ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ διανοίᾳ σου, καὶ τὸν πλησίον σου ὡς σεαυτόν.

records.literal_gloss: And answering he said, You shall love Lord the God of you with all the heart of you and with all the soul of you and with all the strength of you and with all the mind of you, and the neighbor of you as yourself.

en.L: And answering, he said, "'You shall love [the] Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength and with all your mind,' and 'your neighbor as yourself.'"
en.B: He answered, "'You are to love the Lord your God with your whole heart, your whole soul, your whole strength and your whole mind,' and 'your neighbor as you love yourself.'"
en.R: The man answered, "'Love the Lord your God with everything you are: with all your heart, all your soul, all your strength, and all your mind.' And, 'Love your neighbor as much as you love yourself.'"

fr.L: Et, répondant, il dit : « “Tu aimeras le Seigneur ton Dieu de tout ton cœur, et de toute ton âme, et de toute ta force, et de toute ta pensée”, et “ton prochain comme toi-même”. »
fr.B: Il répondit : « “Tu dois aimer le Seigneur ton Dieu de tout ton cœur, de toute ton âme, de toute ta force et de tout ton esprit”, et “ton prochain comme tu t’aimes toi-même”. »
fr.R: L’homme a répondu : « “Aime le Seigneur ton Dieu de tout ton être : de tout ton cœur, de toute ton âme, de toute ta force et de toute ton intelligence.” Et : “Aime ton prochain autant que tu t’aimes toi-même.” »

decisions.choice: Deuteronomy 6:5, with mind added
alternatives: a summary in the expert's own words
decisions.reason: The man quotes the command that follows "Hear, O Israel" (Deuteronomy 6:4-5), which Jews recited daily. The Hebrew has heart, soul and strength; the form here adds the mind, as in Mark 12:30. "Lord" stands for the divine name in the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: Leviticus 19:18: your neighbor as yourself
decisions.reason: The command comes from Leviticus 19, where the neighbor is a fellow Israelite; the same chapter tells Israel to love the foreigner living among them as themselves (Leviticus 19:34). Jesus joins the same two commands in Mark 12:29-31.

decisions.choice: heart, soul, strength, mind: the whole person
alternatives: four separate parts of a person
decisions.reason: Together the words mean every part of one's life: will, feelings, energy and thought.

decisions.choice: you shall love: a command
decisions.reason: The future tense in the law gives a command.

decisions.choice: as you love yourself (B); Love your neighbor as much as you love yourself (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek does not repeat the verb. Balanced and Readable supply "love" so that the second command can be read on its own.

decisions.choice: with everything you are
decisions.reason: Readable sums up the list before giving it.

decisions.choice: quotation marks within the speech
decisions.reason: The man answers by quoting two passages of the law, so the quoted words are marked inside his speech.

decisions.choice: ta pensée (L); ton esprit (B); ton intelligence (R)
decisions.reason: As in Mark 12:30: the word means the mind, the power to think. Literal keeps the close "pensée", Balanced the usual "esprit", Readable the plainest "intelligence".

decisions.choice: L’homme (R)
decisions.reason: English Readable keeps "The man"; French names him too, since the previous record's speaker was Jesus.

source.text: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῷ· Ὀρθῶς ἀπεκρίθης· τοῦτο ποίει καὶ ζήσῃ.

records.literal_gloss: He said then to him, Correctly you answered; this do and you will live.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to him, "You have answered correctly; do this and you will live."
en.B: Jesus told him, "Your answer is right. Do this, and you will live."
en.R: Jesus said, "You are right. If you do this, you will live."

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} lui dit : « Tu as répondu correctement ; fais cela et tu vivras. »
fr.B: Jésus lui dit : « Tu as bien répondu. Fais cela, et tu vivras. »
fr.R: Jésus a dit : « Tu as raison. Si tu fais cela, tu vivras. »

decisions.choice: do this and you will live: echoing Leviticus 18:5
decisions.reason: God told Israel to keep his laws, which a person must do to live (Leviticus 18:5). "You will live" answers the question about eternal life (10:25).

decisions.choice: do: keep on doing
decisions.reason: The present tense means to keep doing it, as a way of life.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speaker.

source.text: Ὁ δὲ θέλων δικαιῶσαι ἑαυτὸν εἶπεν πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν· Καὶ τίς ἐστίν μου πλησίον;

records.literal_gloss: But wanting to justify himself he said to Jesus, And who is my neighbor?

en.L: But wanting to justify himself, he said to Jesus, "And who is my neighbor?"
en.B: But the man wanted to show that he was in the right, so he asked Jesus, "And who counts as my neighbor?"
en.R: But the man wanted to show that he had done nothing wrong. So he asked Jesus, "Who is my neighbor?"

fr.L: Mais lui, voulant se justifier, dit à Jésus : « Et qui est mon prochain ? »
fr.B: Mais l’homme voulait montrer qu’il était dans son droit ; il demanda donc à Jésus : « Et qui est-ce qui compte comme mon prochain ? »
fr.R: Mais l’homme voulait montrer qu’il n’avait rien fait de mal. Alors il a demandé à Jésus : « Qui est mon prochain ? »

decisions.choice: justify himself: show himself to be in the right
decisions.reason: The verb is related to the word for righteousness. Here it means defending himself, as in 16:15: by limiting whom he had to love, or by showing his question was a real one.

decisions.choice: who is my neighbor: how far does the command reach?
decisions.reason: Leviticus 19 speaks of fellow Israelites and of foreigners living in the land. The question asks where the duty to love stops.

decisions.choice: the man
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the subject.

decisions.choice: counts as
decisions.reason: Balanced shows that the question is about who qualifies.

decisions.choice: le prochain, every level, Readable included
decisions.reason: The whole exchange turns on this word (10:27, 29, 36), so Readable keeps "prochain", which French readers know from the commandment, rather than the looser "les autres" Mark 12:31 uses at Readable.

source.text: ὑπολαβὼν δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Ἄνθρωπός τις κατέβαινεν ἀπὸ Ἰερουσαλὴμ εἰς Ἰεριχὼ καὶ λῃσταῖς περιέπεσεν, οἳ καὶ ἐκδύσαντες αὐτὸν καὶ πληγὰς ἐπιθέντες ἀπῆλθον ἀφέντες ἡμιθανῆ.

records.literal_gloss: Taking up Jesus said, A man certain was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and robbers fell among, who both having stripped him and blows having laid on went away having left half dead.

en.L: Taking [this] up, Jesus said, "A certain man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and he fell among robbers, who stripped him and laid blows on [him] and went away, leaving [him] half dead.
en.B: Jesus took up the question and said, "A man was on his way down from Jerusalem to Jericho when robbers set on him. They tore off his clothes, gave him a beating, and went off and left him lying there half dead.
en.R: Jesus answered with a story. "A man was walking down the road from Jerusalem to Jericho. Robbers attacked him. They took his clothes, beat him up, and ran off. They left him lying there, almost dead.

fr.L: Reprenant [la parole], Jésus dit : « Un homme descendait de Jérusalem à Jéricho, et il est tombé sur des brigands, qui, après l’avoir dépouillé et l’avoir roué de coups, sont partis en le laissant à demi mort.
fr.B: Jésus reprit la parole : « Un homme descendait de Jérusalem à Jéricho quand des brigands l’ont attaqué. Ils lui ont arraché ses vêtements, l’ont roué de coups, puis ils sont partis en le laissant à moitié mort.
fr.R: Jésus a répondu par une histoire : « Un homme descendait la route de Jérusalem à Jéricho. Des bandits l’ont attaqué. Ils lui ont pris ses vêtements, ils l’ont frappé, puis ils se sont enfuis. Ils l’ont laissé là, presque mort.

decisions.choice: taking it up: replying to the question
decisions.reason: The verb means to take up what someone has said and answer it.

decisions.choice: going down from Jerusalem to Jericho: a steep road through the desert
decisions.reason: Jerusalem stands high in the hills; Jericho lies near the Jordan, far below. The road ran down through the dry and lonely Judean wilderness, where robbers could attack travelers.

decisions.choice: robbers: bandits who rob by force
decisions.reason: The word means violent bandits, as in "a den of robbers" (19:46).

decisions.choice: half dead: near death
decisions.reason: He was alive but looked as if he might be dead.

decisions.choice: answered with a story
decisions.reason: Readable says that what follows is a story Jesus tells.

decisions.choice: robbers set on him
decisions.reason: Balanced uses an everyday phrase for being attacked.

decisions.choice: the story Jesus tells in the passé composé at every level, with the imperfect for the background ("descendait")
alternatives: passé simple at Literal and Balanced, as in the narration
decisions.reason: The story is part of Jesus's speech, and spoken French tells a story in the passé composé; the style guide (section 9) sets this for the parables at every level. The narrative frame ("Jésus dit", "Jésus reprit la parole") keeps the passé simple at Literal and Balanced.

source.text: κατὰ συγκυρίαν δὲ ἱερεύς τις κατέβαινεν ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ ἐκείνῃ, καὶ ἰδὼν αὐτὸν ἀντιπαρῆλθεν·

records.literal_gloss: By chance now a priest certain was going down on the road that, and having seen him passed by on the other side.

en.L: Now by chance a certain priest was going down on that road, and seeing him, he passed by on the other side.
en.B: It so happened that a priest was traveling down by that same road. He saw the man, but went past him, keeping to the far side.
en.R: It happened that a priest was going down that same road. When he saw the man, he went by on the other side of the road.

fr.L: Or, par hasard, un prêtre descendait par ce chemin-là, et, l’ayant vu, il est passé de l’autre côté.
fr.B: Il s’est trouvé qu’un prêtre descendait par cette même route. Il a vu l’homme, mais il est passé sans s’arrêter, en se tenant de l’autre côté.
fr.R: Par hasard, un prêtre descendait la même route. Quand il a vu l’homme, il est passé de l’autre côté de la route.

decisions.choice: priest: a descendant of Aaron who served at the temple
decisions.reason: Priests served in the temple in turns (1:8-9) and lived in Jerusalem and the towns of Judea. The story gives no reason why he passed by. The law kept priests from making themselves unclean through a dead body (Leviticus 21:1), but the story does not say this was his reason.

decisions.choice: passed by on the other side: went past on the opposite side
decisions.reason: The verb means to go past on the opposite side. He saw the man and kept his distance.

decisions.choice: by chance: as it happened
decisions.reason: The story turns on who happens to come along.

decisions.choice: the man
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear who is seen.

source.text: ὁμοίως δὲ καὶ Λευίτης κατὰ τὸν τόπον ἐλθὼν καὶ ἰδὼν ἀντιπαρῆλθεν.

records.literal_gloss: Likewise now also a Levite having come to the place and having seen passed by on the other side.

en.L: And likewise a Levite also, coming to the place and seeing [him], passed by on the other side.
en.B: A Levite did the same. He came to the spot, saw him, and went past on the far side.
en.R: Then a Levite came to that place. He also saw the man and went by on the other side.

fr.L: Et de même aussi un Lévite, arrivé à cet endroit et [l’]ayant vu, est passé de l’autre côté.
fr.B: Un Lévite a fait de même : il est arrivé à cet endroit, il a vu l’homme et il est passé à l’écart, de l’autre côté.
fr.R: Ensuite, un Lévite est arrivé à cet endroit. Lui aussi a vu l’homme, et il est passé de l’autre côté.

decisions.choice: Levite: a member of the tribe of Levi who helped the priests at the temple
decisions.reason: Levites were descendants of Levi who were not priests. They served at the temple as the priests' helpers, guards and singers (Numbers 3:5-9; 1 Chronicles 23:28-32). Like the priest, he was a man whose work was the service of God.

decisions.choice: likewise also: the same thing happens again
alternatives: the Levite was with the priest
decisions.reason: The second man repeats what the first did, word for word.

decisions.choice: the man
decisions.reason: Readable supplies the object the Greek leaves understood.

source.text: Σαμαρίτης δέ τις ὁδεύων ἦλθεν κατ’ αὐτὸν καὶ ἰδὼν ἐσπλαγχνίσθη, καὶ προσελθὼν κατέδησεν τὰ τραύματα αὐτοῦ ἐπιχέων ἔλαιον καὶ οἶνον, ἐπιβιβάσας δὲ αὐτὸν ἐπὶ τὸ ἴδιον κτῆνος ἤγαγεν αὐτὸν εἰς πανδοχεῖον καὶ ἐπεμελήθη αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: A Samaritan however certain journeying came upon him, and having seen was moved with compassion, \v 34 and having approached bound up the wounds of him pouring on oil and wine, having put then him on the own animal brought him to an inn and took care of him.

en.L: But a certain Samaritan who was traveling came upon him, and seeing [him], he was moved with compassion, \v 34 and coming near he bound up his wounds, pouring on oil and wine, and putting him on his own animal, he brought him to an inn and cared for him.
en.B: Then a Samaritan, who was on a journey, came to where the man lay. When he saw him, his heart went out to him. \v 34 He went over to him, poured oil and wine on his wounds and bound them up. Then he lifted him onto his own animal, took him to an inn, and looked after him.
en.R: But then a Samaritan came along on his travels. When he came to the man and saw him, he felt deeply sorry for him. \v 34 He went over to him. He poured olive oil and wine on the man's wounds and wrapped them up. Then he put the man on his own donkey and took him to an inn. There he took care of him.

fr.L: Mais un certain Samaritain qui était en voyage est arrivé près de lui, et, [l’]ayant vu, il a été pris de compassion ; \v 34 et, s’étant approché, il a bandé ses plaies en y versant de l’huile et du vin ; puis, l’ayant fait monter sur sa propre monture, il l’a conduit à une auberge et a pris soin de lui.
fr.B: Puis un Samaritain, qui était en voyage, est arrivé à l’endroit où l’homme était étendu. Quand il l’a vu, il a été saisi de pitié pour lui. \v 34 Il s’est approché, a versé de l’huile et du vin sur ses plaies et les a bandées. Ensuite il l’a installé sur sa propre bête, l’a emmené dans une auberge et s’est occupé de lui.
fr.R: Mais ensuite, un Samaritain qui voyageait est passé par là. Quand il est arrivé près de l’homme et qu’il l’a vu, il a eu profondément pitié de lui. \v 34 Il s’est approché de lui. Il a versé de l’huile d’olive et du vin sur ses blessures, et il les a entourées de bandes. Puis il a mis l’homme sur son âne et il l’a emmené dans une auberge. Là, il s’est occupé de lui.

decisions.choice: Samaritan: one of the people of Samaria, whom Jews counted as enemies
decisions.reason: Jews and Samaritans were hostile to each other (9:52-53; John 4:9). After a priest and a Levite, the third traveler is not a Jew at all. He is a figure in Jesus's story.

decisions.choice: was moved with compassion: felt a deep pity that led to action
decisions.reason: Luke uses this verb of Jesus at Nain (7:13) and of the father of the lost son (15:20).

decisions.choice: oil and wine: used to treat wounds
alternatives: a meal for the wounded man
decisions.reason: Wine helped to clean a wound, and olive oil soothed it (compare Isaiah 1:6, where wounds have not been softened with oil).

decisions.choice: animal: a beast for riding or carrying loads, probably a donkey
decisions.reason: The word means any domestic animal used for work. The Samaritan walks so that the wounded man can ride.

decisions.choice: inn: a lodging place that took in travelers
alternatives: a guest room in a house
decisions.reason: The word means a place that receives all comers, with a keeper (10:35). It is a different word from the guest room of 2:7.

decisions.choice: poured oil and wine on his wounds and bound them up
alternatives: bound up his wounds, pouring on oil and wine
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the steps in the order they would be done.

decisions.choice: his heart went out to him
decisions.reason: An everyday phrase for deep pity.

decisions.choice: donkey
decisions.reason: Readable names the likely animal (see the meaning decision).

source.text: καὶ ἐπὶ τὴν αὔριον ἐκβαλὼν δύο δηνάρια ἔδωκεν τῷ πανδοχεῖ καὶ εἶπεν· Ἐπιμελήθητι αὐτοῦ, καὶ ὅ τι ἂν προσδαπανήσῃς ἐγὼ ἐν τῷ ἐπανέρχεσθαί με ἀποδώσω σοι.

records.literal_gloss: And on the next day having taken out two denarii he gave to the innkeeper and said, Take care of him, and whatever more you might spend, I in the returning of me will repay you.

en.L: And on the next day, taking out two denarii, he gave [them] to the innkeeper and said, 'Take care of him, and whatever more you spend, I will repay you when I come back.'
en.B: The next day he took out two denarii and handed them to the innkeeper. 'Care for him,' he said, 'and if you spend anything more, I will pay you back on my return.'
en.R: The next day he took out two silver coins and gave them to the man who ran the inn. He said, 'Take care of this man. If it costs you more than this, I will pay you when I come back this way.'

fr.L: Et le lendemain, sortant deux deniers, il [les] a donnés à l’aubergiste et a dit : “Prends soin de lui, et tout ce que tu dépenseras en plus, moi, à mon retour, je te le rembourserai.”
fr.B: Le lendemain, il a sorti deux deniers et les a remis à l’aubergiste. “Occupe-toi de lui, lui a-t-il dit, et si tu dépenses davantage, je te le rendrai à mon retour.”
fr.R: Le lendemain, il a sorti deux pièces d’argent et il les a données au patron de l’auberge. Il lui a dit : “Prends soin de cet homme. Si cela te coûte plus, je te paierai quand je repasserai par ici.”

decisions.choice: two denarii: two days' wages
